extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of the PARI/GP system writing GP scripts or extending the PARI library (mathematicians and scientific programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and reference for writing, debugging and extending PARI/GP code: classified error types, semantics of GP control constructs, and detailed descriptions of GP-specific library functions and their expected usage and side-effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e TYPE"
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument x of function s had an unexpected type (example: factor("blah")).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has two components: 1 (t_STR): the function name s, 2: the offending argument x.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e TYPE2"
rubrics_metrics.description: Forbidden operation between two objects that cannot be typecast to a sensible common domain (example: Mod(1,2) + Pi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has three components: 1 (t_STR) the operator name op, 2: first argument, 3: second argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e PRIORITY"
rubrics_metrics.description: Object o in function s contains variables whose priority is incompatible with the expected operation (example: Pol([x,1], 'y) — coefficients involve variables with higher priority than the main variable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has four components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 the offending argument o, 3 (t_STR) an operator op describing the priority error, 4 (t_POL) the variable v describing the priority error. The argument satisfies variable(x) op variable(v).

rubrics_metrics.name: "e VAR"
rubrics_metrics.description: The variables of arguments x and y submitted to function s do not match up (example: Mod(t,t^2+1) in nfinit(x^2+1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has three components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 (t_POL) argument x, 3 (t_POL) argument y.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e COMPONENT"
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempting to access an inexistent component in a vector/matrix/list: the index is less than 1 or greater than the allowed length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has four components: 1 (t_STR) function name, 2 (t_STR) an operator op (< or >), 3 (t_GEN) a numerical limit l bounding allowed range, 4 (GEN) the index x. It satisfies x op l.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e DOMAIN"
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument is not in the function’s domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has five components: 1 (t_STR) function name, 2 (t_STR) mathematical name of the out-of-domain argument, 3 (t_STR) an operator op describing the domain error, 4 (t_GEN) numerical limit l, 5 (GEN) the out-of-domain argument x. The argument satisfies x op l which prevents membership in domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e MAXPRIME"
rubrics_metrics.description: A function using the precomputed list of prime numbers ran out of primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component: 1 (t_INT) the requested prime bound, which overflew primelimit or is 0 (bound unknown).

rubrics_metrics.name: "e MEM"
rubrics_metrics.description: A call to pari_malloc or pari_realloc failed (memory allocation failure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has no component.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e OVERFLOW"
rubrics_metrics.description: An object in function s becomes too large to be represented within PARI’s hardcoded limits (examples: huge exponentials such as 2^2^2^10 or exp(1e100)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component: 1 (t_STR) the function name s.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e PREC"
rubrics_metrics.description: Function s fails because input accuracy is too low (example: floor(1e100) at default accuracy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component: 1 (t_STR) the function name s.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e STACK"
rubrics_metrics.description: The PARI stack overflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has no component.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e ALARM"
rubrics_metrics.description: A timeout generated by the alarm function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the error message to print. The alarm(timeout, code) can return a t_ERROR if code aborted; example usage shown with timed factorization and time-bounded partial factorizations (alarm used to limit computations and return partial results). Caveat: cannot set a new alarm within alarm code (new timer erases parent).

rubrics_metrics.name: "e USER"
rubrics_metrics.description: A user error as triggered by error(g1, ..., gn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component: 1 (t_VEC) the vector of n arguments given to error.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e CONSTPOL"
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument of function s is a constant polynomial which does not make sense (example: galoisinit(Pol(1))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component: 1 (t_STR) the function name s.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e COPRIME"
rubrics_metrics.description: Function s expected coprime arguments but received x,y which were not coprime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has three components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2: argument x, 3: argument y.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e INV"
rubrics_metrics.description: Tried to invert a non-invertible object x in function s (note: inverting Mod(a,b) when a not 0 mod b can leak factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2: the non-invertible x. Example explains consequence for t_INTMOD allowing factorization via gcd.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e IRREDPOL"
rubrics_metrics.description: Function s expected an irreducible polynomial and received one that was reducible (example: nfinit(x^2-1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 (t_POL) the polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e MISC"
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic uncategorized error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the error message to print.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e MODULUS"
rubrics_metrics.description: Moduli x and y submitted to function s are inconsistent (example: nfalgtobasis(nfinit(t^3-2), Mod(t,t^2+1))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has three components: 1 (t_STR) function s, 2: argument x, 3: argument y.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e PRIME"
rubrics_metrics.description: Function s expected a prime number but received p which was not prime (example: idealprimedec(nf, 4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2: the argument p.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e ROOTS0"
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument of function s is the zero polynomial and the function needs to consider its roots (example: polroots(0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component: 1 (t_STR) the function name s.

rubrics_metrics.name: "e SQRTN"
rubrics_metrics.description: Trying to compute an n-th root of x which does not exist in function s (example: sqrt(Mod(-1,3))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2: the argument x.

rubrics_metrics.name: next({n = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Control construct: interrupts execution of current seq and resumes the next iteration of the innermost enclosing loop (or top-level loop); if n specified, resumes at the n-th enclosing loop; if n > number of enclosing loops all are exited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to control loop flow; semantics similar to 'continue' but supports numeric nesting level.

rubrics_metrics.name: return({x = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns from current subroutine with result x; if x omitted returns void value (like print).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard subroutine return; omit x to return no result.

rubrics_metrics.name: until(a, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq until a is not equal to 0 (i.e. until a is true). The condition is tested after executing seq, so seq runs at least once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantics: post-test loop (do-while style). If a initially non-zero seq is still evaluated once.

rubrics_metrics.name: while(a, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq as long as a is non-zero; the test is before executing seq, so if a initially zero seq is not evaluated at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard pre-test loop semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strprintf(fmt, {x}*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a string built from remaining arguments according to format fmt (see printf for conversions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strings are expanded on the spot; used to format strings in GP.

rubrics_metrics.name: addhelp(sym, str)
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes the help message for symbol sym. The string is expanded and stored as online help for sym. Recommended to document global variables and user functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once addhelp is applied to a function, its code is no longer included in the default help display; help of aliases is not shown (alias expands to target). You can modify built-in help but maintainers would like to be informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: alarm({s = 0}, {code})
rubrics_metrics.description: If code omitted: trigger an e ALARM exception after s seconds, cancelling previous alarms; if code supplied and s positive evaluate code but abort after s seconds, returning the value of code on success or a t_ERROR on timeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to time-limit computations. Example demonstrates partial factorization returned when alarm triggers; note cannot set a new alarm within alarm code (new timer erases parent). Library syntax and examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: alias(newsym, sym)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines symbol newsym as an alias for sym (can alias functions, member functions with '.' prefix, and operators using internal names).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alias is performed at compilation-time and only affects GP code compiled after alias evaluation; does not affect previous definitions — to change earlier behaviour you must redefine functions. Use variables for a slower but runtime-flexible behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: allocatemem({s = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Change stack size after initialization: if x>0 allocate new stack of at least x bytes; if x=0 size of new stack is twice the old one. Behavior depends on parisizemax setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With parisizemax enabled: three sizes matter (parisizemax, parisize, current stack). allocatemem changes current stack up to parisizemax temporarily; useful to reduce garbage collection during big computations. Deprecated behavior when parisizemax unset: synonym for default(parisize,...). Important caveats: allocatemem must be typed at gp prompt (not usable inside sequences/loops as it discards remainder of sequence); increasing stack may move it and longjmp occurs (temporary objects invalid), so sequences after allocatemem are discarded. Use before big computations; changing parisize at break loop may interrupt computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: apply(f, A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply closure f to entries of A: if A scalar return f(A); if polynomial or series apply to coefficients; if vector/list return f(x) for elements; if matrix return matrix of f applied to each entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to map functions over lists/vectors/matrices; many built-ins act componentwise for vectors/matrices but not lists — apply useful for lists. Alternative set-notation shortcuts exist ([g(x)|x<-v,f(x)] etc.). Examples show apply on vectors, matrices, polynomials, and lists (lifting elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: call(f, A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given vector A=[a1,...,an] and f a function, returns evaluation f(a1,...,an). If #A=1, call(f,A)=apply(f,A)[1]. If f variadic, last component should be vector of variadic args.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when writing variadic functions and when dealing with arguments of unspecified arity. Example: fprintf via write+call(Strprintf,[format,args]). Also used to call operators by internal names. Provided memoize example showing caching via map keyed by [f,A].

rubrics_metrics.name: default({key}, {val})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns default corresponding to keyword key; if val present sets default to val (subject to string expansion). default() lists all defaults and values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortcuts and interactive display differences mentioned; see other sections for lists of defaults. Library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: errname(E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the type of the error message E as a string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple utility to inspect error object types.

rubrics_metrics.name: error({str}*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs its argument list (each interpreted as a string), then interrupts running gp program, returning to input prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to trigger user errors with diagnostic messages (example: error("n = ", n, " is not squarefree!")).

rubrics_metrics.name: extern(str) and externstr(str)
rubrics_metrics.description: Run an external shell command named by string str: extern() feeds the command output into gp as if read from a file; externstr() returns a vector of GP strings (one per output line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File and command integration shown; security default may disable fileextern/fileopen variants in some environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: fileclose(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Close file descriptor n created via fileopen or fileextern; closing recycles descriptors and avoids running out of them. For write-opened files, forces a write of buffered data to filesystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quitting gp implicitly calls fileclose on all descriptors. Closing twice raises an exception (invalid descriptor). Use explicit fileclose to avoid data loss in case of crashes; examples show OS limits on open files and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: fileextern(str)
rubrics_metrics.description: Run external command str and return a file descriptor attached to its output (read like a file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage shown with ls; if secure default is set, this function will raise an exception. Use fileclose when done.

rubrics_metrics.name: fileflush({n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Flush file descriptor n: forces write of all buffered data to filesystem and completes pending writes. If n omitted, flush all descriptors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to ensure file contains expected content at synchronization points. fileclose implicitly flushes; examples show periodic flushing in loops to keep files consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: fileopen(path, mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open file at path and return a file descriptor. Modes: 'r' (default) for reading, 'w' for writing (discard existing), 'a' for appending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files should be closed with fileclose; in read mode raise exception if file missing or no permission; in write mode raise exception if cannot write. Attempting read/write with wrong mode raises invalid file descriptor error. Examples demonstrate reading logical vs raw lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: fileread(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Read a logical line from file descriptor n (as prepared by gp preprocessor); return 0 at EOF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A logical line is a full command assembled by preprocessor (skips blanks/comments and assembles multiline commands). Contrast with filereadstr which reads raw line up to newline. Examples show difference between raw and logical lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: filereadstr(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Read a raw line from file descriptor n, discarding terminating newline — exact input up to next '\n'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use filereadstr for raw-line reading; fileread returns logical lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: filewrite(n, s) and filewrite1(n, s)
rubrics_metrics.description: filewrite writes string s to descriptor n ending with newline; filewrite1 writes s without adding newline. Files must be opened in 'w' or 'a' mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No guarantee data reaches disk until fileclose; use fileflush/fileclose to sync. For large numbers of writes low-level fileopen/filewrite is far more efficient than repeated high-level write operations — examples show timing differences. To append newline with filewrite1 use Str(s, "\n").

rubrics_metrics.name: fold(f, A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply binary closure f to entries of A left-associatively to return f(...f(f(A[1],A[2]),A[3])...,A[#A]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for reductions (product, combining) and examples show numeric and higher-order uses (composition of functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: getabstime(), gettime(), getwalltime()
rubrics_metrics.description: Time utilities: getabstime() returns CPU time (ms) since gp startup (reentrant); gettime() returns CPU time (ms) used since last call or beginning of containing instruction; getwalltime() returns wall-clock ms since Unix epoch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use getabstime for reentrant timing; getwalltime for wall-clock measurements; examples show measuring elapsed time for segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: getenv(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return value of environment variable s if defined, otherwise return 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to adapt scripts to environment configuration.

rubrics_metrics.name: getheap()
rubrics_metrics.description: Return two-component row vector: number of objects on heap and amount of memory they occupy (in long words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mainly for debugging memory usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: getrand() and setrand/getrand semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: getrand() returns current value of seed used by RNG (technical internal state) useful for reproducing computations; value is technical and only meaningful to setrand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for debugging and reproducing pseudo-random sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: getstack()
rubrics_metrics.description: Return current value of top - avma (bytes used on stack so far).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for debugging stack usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: global(listof variables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete function; scheduled for deletion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use; retain for backward compatibility only.

rubrics_metrics.name: inline(x, ..., z)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Experimental) declare x,...,z as inline variables which behave like lexically scoped variables but with unlimited scope; can exit scope with uninline().
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When used in GP scripts, call uninline() before script end to avoid leaking inline variables outside the script.

rubrics_metrics.name: input()
rubrics_metrics.description: Reads a string interpreted as GP expression from input file (usually keyboard); if sequence of expressions given returns result of last expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using under pari.el with Emacs, prompt string must end with same prompt as previous ones; often used with print1 to prompt user. Library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: install(name, code, {gpname}, {lib})
rubrics_metrics.description: Loads from dynamic library lib the function name and assigns it name gpname in current gp session with prototype code; gives access to non-static PARI library functions or external functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Powerful but system-dependent: may segfault when gp statically linked. Prototype encoding: first char i/l/v for return type, letters for argument types (G,&,L,s,n), p/P for precisions, DG/D&/Dn for optional args. Re-installing warns and updates prototype but does not reload library symbol. Caution: test on harmless example first; examples show installing addii and calling it.

rubrics_metrics.name: kill(sym)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restore symbol sym to undeclared status and delete help messages attached by addhelp. Killing a variable does not remove its name from variable list or change priority; kill is the only way to remove aliases and installed functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Killing user functions removes aliases/installed functions; alternative ' 'quote to reset variable to initial value keeps help message. Examples illustrate behavior and that names remain in variable list.

rubrics_metrics.name: listcreate({n}), listinsert(L,x,n), listkill(L), listpop(list,{n}), listput(list,x,{n}), listsort(L,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: List operations: create empty List (use List instead of listcreate); listinsert inserts at position n (O(#L-n+1)); listkill obsolete; listpop removes n-th element or last if omitted; listput sets n-th element or appends if n omitted; listsort sorts list in place according to universal cmp and if flag non-zero suppress repeated coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: listput can append beyond end and will reallocate list if needed (amortized O(1) per append); repeated listputs overall cost O(#L). listsort is faster than vecsort because in-place, and sorted list can use setsearch. Examples show exceptions on invalid indices and behavior when inserting beyond end.

rubrics_metrics.name: localbitprec(p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set real precision to p bits in dynamic scope: computations use p bits for transcendental constants and conversions; realbitprecision itself is unaffected and unmasked when exiting scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to masking default(realbitprecision) in dynamic scope but safer; nested scopes allowed; note precision increments step by 64 (32 on 32-bit) so p rounded to multiple of that step. Changing realbitprecision in programs is deprecated; localbitprec follows dynamic (not lexical) scoping rules; subroutines called from localbitprec use local accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: localprec(p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set real precision to p decimal digits in dynamic scope: computations use p digits for transcendental constants and conversions; realprecision itself is unaffected and unmasked when exiting scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safer alternative to changing default(realprecision) inside programs; nested localprec statements allowed. Warning: mixing realprecision and localprec leads to surprising results because realprecision is ignored within localprec scope and not restored.
